title: Monorepo Management
summary: Sets up and maintains a TypeScript monorepo with workspaces, shared configs, task caching and CI that builds only the packages a change affects.
description: A monorepo helps when packages share code and hurts when every pull request rebuilds everything. This skill sets the boundaries first: what is a package, who may import whom, and which tasks run where.
It then wires workspaces, one shared TypeScript base config and a task runner with caching, so CI time follows the size of the change rather than the size of the repository.
useWhen: You are splitting one app into apps and shared packages
CI takes longer every month because it rebuilds all packages
Packages import each other through relative paths into src folders
Versions of the same dependency differ between packages
body:
# Monorepo management

Structure decides cost. Fix the graph before the tooling.

## Layout

- `apps/*` for deployables, `packages/*` for libraries. Apps depend on packages; packages never depend on apps; a package depending on another package is declared, never reached by a relative path.
- Use the package manager's workspaces (pnpm, npm or yarn) with the `workspace:*` protocol for internal dependencies. One lockfile at the root.

## Steps

1. Map the current graph: each package's name, its internal dependencies and its scripts. Report cycles and fix them by extracting the shared part into a third package.
2. Shared config goes in packages: `tsconfig.base.json` extended by each package, one ESLint config, one formatter config. Packages use TypeScript project references (`composite: true`) when builds are separate, or point `exports` at built output.
3. Every package exposes the same scripts: `build`, `test`, `lint`, `typecheck`. Add a task runner (Turborepo or Nx): declare `dependsOn: ["^build"]`, list inputs and outputs per task, and enable the cache.
4. Dependencies: keep versions aligned across packages (a `catalog` in pnpm, or syncpack). Put tools in the root only when every package uses them.
5. CI: run only affected tasks, for example `turbo run build test --filter=...[origin/main]`, and cache between runs. Keep a full run on the default branch.
6. Releases: use changesets or similar so each package versions on its own when it needs to.

## Rules

- Never add a path alias that reaches into another package's `src`.
- Verify with a clean install and `build` from scratch before you finish.

## Report

The graph before and after, config added, and CI time with and without the cache.

example.prompt: Split our web app into a monorepo with a shared ui package and an api package
example.result: Created apps/web and apps/api, packages/ui and packages/config with pnpm workspaces. Removed 14 relative imports into other src folders. Turborepo runs build and test with caching; a ui-only change now rebuilds 2 of 4 packages. Clean install plus full build passes.

faq.question: Which tools does it pick?
faq.answer: It keeps whatever you already use. For a fresh setup it suggests pnpm workspaces with Turborepo, and asks before installing.

faq.question: Is a monorepo always the right choice?
faq.answer: No. With no shared code and separate release schedules, separate repositories are simpler. The skill says so when the graph shows that.

access: Reads package manifests and configs across the repository
Edits workspace config, tsconfigs and CI files; runs install and build
